purpose: Determine whether Kaggle GPU accelerates the registered small-batch workload without silently changing task, optimization, dtype or test access
provider: Kaggle private kernel, user-selected available quota
training_authorization: First submit engineering preflight only; full 72-trial grid and fresh twenty-seed evaluation are not launched by the preflight
fixtures: dev030-engineering-fixture only; no scientific train/validation/test episodes
precision: FP32; no AMP, TF32, compilation or batch-size changes; deterministic CUDA settings
training_trajectories: CPU and CUDA training are separate runtime cohorts. Initial/one-step parity is not a guarantee of identical long-run optimization. Do not merge runtime cohorts silently.
event_table: Public deterministic state updates stay on CPU; learned prediction head on selected device. Hybrid placement explicitly recorded.
recommendation: GPU training candidate only if all parity checks pass and sum of per-arm median end-to-end update times is at least 20% faster than CPU. Recommendation is engineering-only, not architecture selection; no scientific outcome is inspected.
evidence: Frozen git source, protocol hashes, full per-arm CPU/GPU latency samples, initial/post-update discrepancies, exact decision checks, runtime/device metadata and no-test-access declaration
limitations: No GPU validation is claimed from a CPU-only fixture. No quota, speedup, accelerator type or completed remote run may be assumed without observed evidence. GPU quota and API authentication are distinct.
